today.h: The Barrel Relents: Oil Off Its Five-Month High, the Dow Up 1% — and the Nasdaq Flat
today.d: A diplomatic headline met a five-month oil high: Brent settled below $109, the 10Y fell 3bp, and 10 of 11 sector ETFs closed green — but chips kept the Nasdaq at zero.
today.c1: Oil gave back its five-month high, and everything rate-sensitive caught the bid. Brent touched $111.99 — its highest since May — before settling at $108.79 (-0.7%), and WTI's expiring November contract settled $101.79 (-1.8%) after a $110.48 session high, once reports said mediators had put a proposal to revive US-Iran talks on the table. The S&P 500 rose 0.28% to 7,712.57 after an opening dip of 0.3% and a 7,747 midmorning peak; the Dow jumped 529.85 points (1.02%) to 52,495.88; the Nasdaq finished 6.07 points lower (-0.02%) at 26,424.82, having been up 0.6% at 10:30. Ten of 11 sector ETFs closed higher — health care +2.4%, real estate +1.7%, utilities +1.3% — with tech the lone loser (-0.3%) and SOXX -0.4%; the equal-weighted RSP rose 1.15% against SPY's 0.34%, and the Russell 2000 gained 1.65%. The 10Y fell 3bp to 5.12% and the 30Y 6bp to 5.42% after housing starts (-5.2%) and pending home sales (-7.3%, the lowest since 2001) left next week's hike odds at 14.9%. The dollar slipped 0.3% to 101.7, gold fell 0.5% to $4,141, bitcoin rose 1.1% to $82.8k and the VIX dropped 6.1% to 17.31. After the bell, SpaceX reported its first profit; Netflix slipped on slower revenue growth.
today.c4:
• The tell was breadth, not the index: RSP +1.15% against SPY's 0.34%, and 10 of 11 sectors green — this was a rotation into everything AI is not, not a fresh leg of the AI trade.
  • Oil is now the swing factor for rates: a $3 pullback in Brent bought 3bp on the 10Y and 1.7% in REITs — $112 is the level that re-tightens the whole chain.
  • The rally rests on an unverified report: both WSJ and Bloomberg flagged that the peace-talk headlines were unconfirmed, so a denial puts $110+ crude straight back in play.
  • Wednesday is the AI trade's real test: Meta and Tesla report, with SpaceX's first profit already on the tape — watch capex guidance, not the headline EPS.

chains.t: ① The Barrel Relents: From $111.99 to $108.79 — and a 3bp Gift to the Long End
steps: The high: Brent touched $111.99, its highest since May, and WTI's expiring November contract $110.48, as Houthi strikes hit an Aramco site in Yanbu, the Shaybah field and the airports in Riyadh and Abha

The turn: reports that mediators had presented a proposal to revive US-Iran talks — unverified — took Brent to a $108.79 settle (-0.7%) and November WTI to $101.79 (-1.8%); December WTI settled $97.82 (-0.7%)
The rates leg: the 10Y fell 3bp to 5.12% and the 30Y 6bp to 5.42%, long Treasuries outperforming as weak housing data did the work
The equity leg: 10 of 11 sector ETFs closed green — health care +2.4%, real estate +1.7%, utilities +1.3% — and the Dow added 529.85 points (1.02%) to 52,495.88
The scoreboard: the S&P 500 +0.28% to 7,712.57 after a 0.3% opening dip, the equal-weighted RSP +1.15% against SPY's 0.34%, and the VIX -6.1% to 17.31
chains.d: The chain: a five-month high in the barrel met a diplomatic headline, the barrel gave the gain back, the long end rallied with it, and everything AI is not did the rest.

news.fact: Brent crude futures settled down 76 cents, or 0.69%, at $108.79. Earlier in the session, the front-month contract reached $111.99, a five-month high. The November contract for US West Texas Intermediate crude, which expired on Tuesday, settled down $1.87, or 1.8%, at $101.79. That was down from the session high of $110.48. The more active December contract settled down 72 cents at $97.82 a barrel.
Stocks got a boost from reports, unverified by The Wall Street Journal, that mediators had presented a proposal to revive talks between the U.S. and Iran.
The 10-year Treasury yield closed at 5.12%, down from 5.15%, and the 30-year at 5.42% from 5.48%, according to the Treasury's daily yield curve.
About 400 companies in the S&P 500 rose, erasing the index's earlier decline. A bounce in chipmakers also helped sentiment. Brent oil fell below $109 a barrel.
The S&P 500 rose 21.84 points to 7,712.57. The Dow Jones Industrial Average rallied 529.85 to 52,495.88, and the Nasdaq composite slipped 6.07 to 26,424.82.

chains.t: ② The AI Ceiling: a 32% Seoul Debut, a Flat Chip Tape — and a Nasdaq That Ended at Zero
steps: The Asian signal: Elice, a South Korean AI-infrastructure supplier, fell 32% in its Seoul debut — the country's worst opening day for a sizeable company — and the Kospi dropped 3.7%, with MSCI's Asia gauge at its lowest since July
The US echo: SOXX was down 1.5% premarket and closed -0.4%; tech was the only one of 11 sector ETFs in the red (-0.3%)
The intraday swing: the Nasdaq fell 0.9% to 26,192 in the first fifteen minutes, was up 0.6% by 10:30, and closed at 26,424.82 — 6.07 points lower
The credit file stayed open: CoreWeave's five-year CDS held near 1,121bp, above the 1,000 distress line, even as the stock rose 1.7%; memory names bounced (WDC +3.4%, STX +2.2%, MRVL +1.4%)
The tell: the selling was confined to the AI complex — the rest of the tape absorbed it without an index-level drawdown
chains.d: The split: the AI complex lost its bid in Asia and never fully got it back in New York — the cap-weighted index stalled while the average stock rose.

news.fact: The latest evidence that investors are questioning the outlook for AI: Elice Inc., a South Korean AI computing supplier scarcely known outside its home market until this week, tanked 32% in its debut in Seoul Tuesday.

The AI infrastructure provider plunged 32 per cent, suffering the country's worst opening day for a sizeable company. MSCI Inc's benchmark for Asia touched its lowest level since July, with South Korea's Kospi index falling 3.7 per cent.

Investor concerns over CoreWeave's credit ticked higher on Tuesday, with the spread on its five-year credit default swap rising back up near levels seen on Thursday. The CDS last saw spreads over 1,121, which is more than 17% higher over the past week. Spreads of 1,000 or greater are generally considered a sign of distress.

Some AI-related stocks staged a bit of a comeback as the session went on. Western Digital gained more than 3%, while Seagate Technology was up more than 2%. CoreWeave and Marvell Technology each advanced more than 1%.
The S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite began Tuesday's session in the red. The broad market index fell 0.2% just after 9:30 a.m. ET, while the tech-heavy Nasdaq pulled back 0.4%.

chains.t: ③ The Earnings Ledger: 3M, Defense and Pharma Paid; GM and GE Did Not
steps: The winners: 3M +5.8%, the Dow's biggest percentage gainer, after topping estimates, raising full-year guidance and expanding a data-center partnership with Amazon; Northrop Grumman +4.6% on an earnings beat

The health-care bid: Eli Lilly +3.5% as the drug group repriced the European committee's 10/16 endorsement of its oral obesity pill; Amgen +3.3%, Merck +3.3%, UnitedHealth +3.0% and J&J +2.2% followed, making health care the best sector at +2.4%
The losers: GM -6.8% despite a beat and a new $20 billion buyback, as it narrowed its profit outlook; GE Aerospace -3.7% on a revenue miss
The idiosyncratic: Hasbro +11.2% on a Magic: The Gathering-driven beat and a doubled buyback target; Equifax +11.3% on an earnings beat even as it trimmed revenue guidance
The net: beats were bought where guidance rose and sold where it narrowed — the Dow's 530 points were built in industrials, defense and health care, not in technology
chains.d: The ledger: this was a stock-picker's tape — good guidance got paid, narrow guidance got sold, and the blue-chip gain came from outside the AI complex.

news.fact: 3M Co. topped profit estimates and raised its full-year outlook for the second straight quarter as the maker of Scotch tape and Post-it notes works to rejuvenate its operations.
General Motors Co. tumbled as shareholders looked past plans for another $20 billion in stock repurchases and focused instead on a narrower profit outlook reflecting sliding sales.

Shares of aerospace and defense company Northrop Grumman advanced more than 4% after it posted an earnings beat. Shares of industrial and safety products producer 3M jumped more than 5% following better-than-expected earnings results and a full-year guidance raise.

A European regulatory endorsement for an oral obesity pill is lifting Eli Lilly stock ahead of the rest of the drug group. Drug and biotechnology stocks are rising broadly alongside Eli Lilly shares, with the iShares Biotechnology ETF up 2%.

In post-earnings moves, General Motors and GE Aerospace ranked among the biggest S&P 500 decliners. 3M rose 6% to lead the Dow, and defense contractors RTX and Northrop Grumman slipped less than 1% and rose 5%, respectively.

chains.t: ④ The Fed File: 14.9%, a Housing Crack — and a 2-Year That Would Not Budge
steps: The data: housing starts fell 5.2% to a 1.22 million annual rate against a 1.3 million estimate; single-family starts ran at 859,000 (-4.6%); permits held at 1.4 million
The crack: pending home sales fell 7.3% to 66.0, the lowest since the series began in 2001
The repricing: CME FedWatch put the odds of a 25bp hike at next week's meeting at 14.9%, down from 22.1% a week ago and 57.6% a month earlier
The curve: the 10Y -3bp to 5.12% and the 30Y -6bp to 5.42%, but the 2Y rose 2bp to 4.79% — a long-end rally, not an easing
The cross-asset check: the dollar -0.3% to 101.7 and gold -0.5% to $4,141 — both softer, neither pricing a pivot
chains.d: The rate file: weak housing did what hawkish talk could not — hike odds fell to 14.9% and the long end rallied, while the front end still edged higher.

news.fact: The Commerce Department reported Tuesday that privately owned starts totaled 1.22 million at a seasonally adjusted annualized rate. That was off 5.2% from the August level and well below the Dow Jones consensus for 1.3 million. Single-family starts totaled 859,000, off 4.6% from the prior month.
The National Association of Realtors said its pending home sales index tumbled 7.3% to 66.0 last month, the lowest level since the series started in 2001.

Traders see a 14.9% probability of a Federal Reserve rate hike of at least 25 basis points at its policy meeting next week, according to CME FedWatch, down from 22.1% a week ago and 57.6% a month earlier.
The 2-year Treasury yield closed at 4.79% versus 4.77% the prior session, while the 10-year fell to 5.12% from 5.15%, per the Treasury's daily yield curve.

chains.t: ⑤ The Cushion: an Earnings Beat, an Open Channel — and Two Prints Next Week
steps: The earnings cushion: SpaceX posted its first profit as a public company after the bell, with revenue more than doubling, and the shares rose 2%; Netflix slipped as revenue growth came in slow

The diplomatic channel: Iran's standing offer — reopen Hormuz within seven days under Iranian control in exchange for lifting the maritime blockade, easing oil sanctions, releasing frozen assets and ending hostilities — remains on the table through Qatari mediators

The counterweight: three senior Iranian officials told Reuters Tehran is deliberately prolonging talks to weaken Trump before the Nov 3 midterms, and Iranian media said there would be no talks until its seven conditions are met
The calendar: Meta and Tesla report Wednesday; the FOMC meets Oct 27-28 and the PCE print lands Oct 29
The floor: the S&P 500 has not closed below 7,650 in any session since Sept 30 — every dip this month has found a bid above that line
chains.d: The cushion: earnings are still beating, the diplomatic channel is open but unverified, and the two prints that decide the quarter are still a week away.

news.fact: SpaceX shares rose 2% after the company reported revenue more than doubled in its second earnings report as a public company. Netflix also reported earnings; shares are slipping after revenue growth came in slow.

Iran's proposal, conveyed through Qatari mediators, offered to reopen the strait within seven days, albeit under Iranian control, provided that Washington lifted its maritime blockade, eased restrictions on Iranian oil exports, released frozen assets and ended hostilities on all fronts.

Iran has deliberately prolonged talks with the US to try to weaken Donald Trump politically ahead of November's US midterm elections, senior officials say, while fears of renewed military action and deep distrust of Washington have reinforced Tehran's reluctance to strike a quick deal.

Iran told Pakistan's army chief on Tuesday that there would be no talks with Washington until Tehran's demands were met, Iranian media reported, underscoring its hardening stance despite mediation efforts by key interlocutor Pakistan.
Despite inaccurate reports that a peace agreement between the US and Iran is close, talks aimed at reaching a deal continue, according to a diplomat involved in negotiations.

mtd.h: October, Fourteen Sessions In: +0.80%, One Record — and a 16-Point Spread
mtd.d: S&P 7,651.5 to 7,712.57 (+0.80% MTD): 1.4% below the 10/6 record, with Energy +10.5% and Tech -5.3% doing the month's work.
mtd.c1: Fourteen sessions into October and the S&P is +0.80% at 7,712.57 — still 1.4% below the 7,818.93 record set on 10/6 — while the Nasdaq is -1.62% and the Dow +3.12%. The month's arc: one record close in the first week, three repricings (wireless on 10/9, the AI complex on 10/12-13, the CPI-PPI pair on 10/14-15), then a chip-led repair that stopped the slide. The 10Y touched a 24-year high of 5.36% on 10/7 and closed at 5.12% (-17bp MTD); October hike odds went from 22% before CPI to a 37% peak and back to 14.9%. Beneath the index: Energy +10.5% leads, Tech -5.3% lags — a ~16-point spread — and eight of 11 sectors are positive. Oil: WTI +12.6% (November), Brent +11.0% (December). Gates: FOMC Oct 27-28, PCE Oct 29.
mtd.c4:
• October's shape is a round trip, not a trend: +0.80% MTD but 1.4% below the 10/6 record — the month's gains were made in the first week and defended since.
  • The dispersion trade still pays: Energy +10.5% against Tech -5.3% is a ~16-point spread — own the barrel's beneficiaries, rent the AI complex until its funding costs stop rising.
  • The month's last gate is the PCE print on Oct 29, the day after the Fed decides: 14.9% October odds price a hold, so the risk is December (~92%) — watch the 10Y at 5.12% through both.

chains.t: ① October's Round Trip: a Record, Three Repricings — and a Chip Repair That Held
steps: The high: 7,818.93 on 10/6 — the S&P's only record close of the month and its first close above 7,800; the index has not been back
The repricings: wireless on 10/9, the AI complex on 10/12-13 and the CPI-PPI pair on 10/14-15 — three separate de-ratings between 10/7 and 10/15
The yield arc: 5.29% at the month's start, 5.36% on 10/7 — a 24-year high — and 5.12% now, a net -17bp
The repair: chips ended a nine-session slide on 10/19 and held most of the gain, but Tech is still -5.3% MTD
The sum: +0.80% MTD, 1.4% below the record — a round trip, not a new leg
chains.d: October so far: one record, three repricings, one repair — the index is roughly level, the leadership is not.

news.fact: The S&P 500 closed above 7,800 for the first time — up 0.6% on the day — and the Nasdaq set another record close; the Dow remains just over 5% shy of its Aug. 5 record.
The 10-year Treasury yield topped 5.30% earlier this month and touched its highest level since 2002.
Shares of the country's largest telecommunications giants are slumping amid worries about growing competition from SpaceX.
Chip stocks rallied Monday, on pace to end a nine-day losing streak. In midday trading, the VanEck Semiconductor ETF climbed nearly 3%, fresh off nine consecutive losing days.

chains.t: ② The Month's Split: Energy +10.5%, Tech -5.3%
steps: Sector map: eight of 11 sectors are positive, led by Energy +10.5%, Staples +8.9%, Health +6.8%, Utilities +6.2% and ConsDisc +6.1%
The gap: the best-to-worst spread is ~16 points — Energy +10.5% against Tech -5.3%
The index math: Dow +3.12% against Nasdaq -1.62%, a 4.7-point gap between the old economy and the AI complex
The size penalty: the equal-weighted S&P is +3.8% MTD against the cap-weighted +0.80% — breadth has outpaid market cap by nearly 3 points
The message: money rotated, it did not leave — eight sectors green, the S&P positive, the Nasdaq down
chains.d: October's split: the barrel and the defensives got paid, the AI complex paid the rent — a rotation, not an exit.

news.fact: Slightly more than half of the stocks in the S&P 500 fell, but all but seven of the 75 stocks in the index's tech sector closed lower. Among the biggest decliners were chip companies, reflecting mounting worries about how long the frenzy over the AI buildout will last.

An outperformance of the so-called quality factor and a decline in the equal-weighted version of the S&P 500 are set to come to an end, providing an opportune window to snap up stocks, Morgan Stanley's Michael Wilson said.

chains.t: ③ The Barrel, Fourteen Sessions In: $98 to $112 and Back
steps: The path: Brent's December contract began October near $98, crossed $100 on 10/1, held a $100-107 corridor for two weeks, then ran to $111.99
The drivers: Hormuz attack counts, strikes on Saudi energy sites and a diesel deal kept re-arming the premium
The offsets: the IEA's diesel warning, a 17-million-barrel SPR offer and the 10/16 Russia waiver
The scoreboard: Brent $108.79 (+11.0% MTD) and WTI $101.79 (+12.6%, November) — both still above $100
The shape: every dip was bought, but the month's high has not been confirmed twice — a war premium policy can dent, not break
chains.d: October's barrel: war kept re-arming the premium, policy kept capping it — a $100-112 month with no resolution.

news.fact: Brent crude futures settled $3.94, or 3.7%, higher at $109.86, the highest since May 19, while US West Texas Intermediate crude futures closed $3.44, or 3.5%, higher at $101.41, the highest since September 17.
On Friday, the U.S. offered up to 17 million barrels from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve, the Department of Energy said.
Brent for December settlement fell 0.3% to settle at $109.55 a barrel. WTI for November delivery gained 2.2% to settle at $103.66; the more-active December contract was down 0.5% to settle at $98.54.

qtd.h: Q4's Opening Ledger: +0.80% Banked, a 5.36% Print — and Four Gates Still Ahead
qtd.d: From 9/30's 7,651.5 to 7,712.57 (+0.80% QTD): the quarter has banked one record and one yield spike, and none of its big gates.
qtd.c1: Q4 is fourteen sessions old. The S&P sits at 7,712.57, +0.80% on the quarter, with the Nasdaq -1.62% and the Dow +3.12%; that compares with a +2.0% third quarter for the S&P, so the quarter has added less than half of what the summer did. What is in the ledger: an all-time closing high of 7,818.93 on 10/6, a 24-year intraday high of 5.36% on the 10Y on 10/7 — now 5.12%, a net -17bp — and three repricings (telecom, the AI complex, the inflation prints) all booked inside the first two weeks. What is not: the FOMC on Oct 27-28, the PCE print on Oct 29, the bulk of Q3 earnings with Meta and Tesla on Wednesday, and the Nov 3 midterms. Brent is +11.0% for the quarter and WTI +12.6%. The quarter's test is whether +0.80% survives those four gates.
qtd.c4:
• The quarter has banked +0.80% and a 24-year yield print, not a direction — the S&P is 1.4% below its 10/6 record with the four biggest gates still unplayed.
  • Position for the calendar, not the tape: FOMC on Oct 27-28, PCE on Oct 29, a megacap earnings week and the midterms — the quarter's whole risk budget sits in the next fourteen days.
  • The rate bill is the swing: a 10Y at 5.12% keeps leadership narrow; a break back below 5% would let the AI complex's repair widen into a quarter-end bid.

chains.t: ① Fourteen Sessions In: What Q4 Has Banked and What It Owes
steps: Banked: a 7,818.93 close on 10/6, the quarter's only record, and a 5.36% print on the 10Y on 10/7, the highest in 24 years
Banked: a full round trip in October hike odds — 22% before CPI, 37% at the peak, 14.9% now
Owed: an FOMC decision on Oct 27-28, with December odds near 92% implying one more hike this year
Owed: the Q3 earnings verdict, tracking 29% growth, with Meta and Tesla reporting Wednesday
The standing: +0.80% QTD on a +2.0% Q3 base — the quarter has added less than half of the summer's gain
chains.d: Q4's first fourteen sessions banked a record and a yield spike — the verdict still sits with the Fed and the earnings week.

news.fact: The S&P 500 closed above 7,800 for the first time — up 0.6% on the day — and the Nasdaq set another record close.
Analysts are forecasting overall growth of 29% for companies in the S&P 500 from the prior summer, according to FactSet.
Results are due from Meta Platforms and Tesla on 10/21, which will kick off Magnificent 7 reports for the latest quarter.

chains.t: ② The Quarter's Rate Bill: 5.12% and a Flatter Long End
steps: The 10Y opened Q4 at 5.29%, printed 5.36% on 10/7 and sits at 5.12% — a net -17bp, but still above 5%
The curve: the 30Y is down 22bp on the quarter, while the 2Y rose 2bp in the latest session — long-end relief, front-end stickiness
The cost: mortgage REITs remain near their lowest since April 2020, the cleanest read on what a 5% long end does to leveraged carry
The offset: Q3 earnings are tracking 29% while the 10Y sits above 5% — the equity case rests on earnings outrunning the long end
The gate: the Oct 27-28 FOMC is the quarter's first decision; December odds near 92% are where the risk lives
chains.d: The quarter's rate bill: a 10Y that touched 5.36% and still sits above 5% — the bull's tax, and the reason leadership is narrow.

news.fact: The 10-year Treasury yield topped 5.30% earlier this month and touched its highest level since 2002.
The iShares Mortgage Real Estate Capped ETF hit a low of $16.71, its lowest level since April 6, 2020; it has fallen more than 24% this year.
According to the CME's FedWatch Tool, traders are pricing in a 16 per cent chance of a rate hike this month and a 92 per cent chance of an increase in December.

chains.t: ③ The Quarter's Calendar: Two Prints, One Earnings Week, One Election
steps: Oct 27-28: the FOMC — October odds 14.9%, December near 92%
Oct 29: PCE, the inflation series the Fed watches, one day after the meeting
Oct 21: Meta and Tesla, the first Magnificent Seven prints of the quarter
Nov 3: the midterms — energy prices and the Russia diesel deal are campaign issues
The rest of Q4: whether +0.80% becomes a base or a peak
chains.d: Q4's next gates — FOMC, PCE, megacap earnings, midterms — decide whether +0.80% is a base or a peak.

news.fact: The Federal Reserve's communications blackout period runs from Oct 17 through Oct 29, ahead of the Oct 27-28 FOMC meeting, according to the Atlanta Fed's 2026 blackout calendar.
Results are due from Netflix and SpaceX after the closing bell on 10/20, followed on 10/21 by Meta Platforms and Tesla, which will kick off Magnificent 7 reports for the latest quarter.
Trump's decision came not long after he said earlier this month he had reached a diesel deal with Russia in an attempt to bring down elevated U.S. fuel prices ahead of the Nov. 3 midterm elections.

ytd.h: The Bull at +12.67%: AI Earnings Carry, a 96bp Rate Bill
ytd.d: S&P +12.67%, Nasdaq +13.69%, Dow +9.22% with fourteen Q4 sessions logged — AI capex and 29% earnings growth carry; a 10Y up 96bp, a 79% barrel and a hot CPI-PPI pair tax the rest.
ytd.c1: The year's base case still holds: AI capex and earnings carry the S&P to +12.67% (7,712.57) and the Nasdaq to +13.69%, with the Dow +9.22%; the bull turned four on 10/12. Against it: a 10Y at 5.12% (+96bp YTD, with a 24-year high of 5.36% printed on 10/7), Brent +78.8% and WTI +77.3% as the war grinds through an eighth month, and a hot September CPI (3.7%) and PPI (6.3%). Beneath the index: Energy +52.0% leads the year, Tech +28.8%, Health +16.2%; Comms -6.4% and ConsDisc -3.3% lag, Utilities -1.9%. Gold -4.6%, bitcoin -5.4%, the dollar +3.5%; December hike odds near 92%.
ytd.c4:
• The year's engine is intact: AI capex and 29% earnings growth have carried the S&P +12.67% through a 96bp rise in the 10Y — earnings are doing the work rates used to do.
  • The credit file is the newest risk: CoreWeave's CDS above 1,000 and Anthropic's valuation reset are the market's stress gauges — watch them before the AI complex.
  • The year's last macro gate is December (odds near 92%): a pause this month is priced; the December decision is where the bull's 2027 setup gets set.

steps: The engines: AI capex — hyperscalers are heading toward $1 trillion a year — and earnings, with Q3 growth tracking 29%
The scoreboard: S&P +12.67%, Nasdaq +13.69%, Dow +9.22% — the AI-heavy index still leads despite October's repricing
The referee: the 10Y at 5.12%, +96bp YTD, and a 24-year high of 5.36% printed on 10/7
The taxes: WTI +77.3% and Brent +78.8% as the war grinds into an eighth month; September CPI 3.7% and PPI 6.3%
The breadth: Energy +52.0% leads; Comms -6.4%, ConsDisc -3.3% and Utilities -1.9% lag
chains.d: The year's base case: AI and earnings compound, rates and oil tax — a four-year bull still faster than its referee.

news.fact: Chipmakers, which have soared over 80% so far this year, were clear underperformers on the day, falling 3.4%.

The bull market turned four on Monday, with many strategists expecting more room for stocks to run. However, concerns over an AI bubble, elevated Treasury yields, and geopolitical uncertainty present hurdles.

The S&P 500 rose 21.84 points to 7,712.57, the Dow rallied 529.85 to 52,495.88 and the Nasdaq slipped 6.07 to 26,424.82. Analysts are forecasting overall growth of 29% for S&P 500 companies, according to FactSet.

chains.t: ② The Rate and Inflation Tax
steps: The long end: the 10Y from 4.16% to 5.12% (+96bp); the 30Y from 4.84% to 5.42% (+58bp)
The Fed: a September hike, its first since July 2023 — with December odds near 92%
The prints: September CPI 3.7% y/y and PPI 6.3% y/y; October hike odds round-tripped 22% to 37% and back to 14.9%
The cross-asset echo: the dollar +3.5%, gold -4.6% — real rates, not war, set the tone for both
chains.d: 2026's tax: a 96bp rise in the 10Y and a second inflation wave — the September hike was the year's regime change.

news.fact: Tight global crude supplies during the Iran war have sent US crude soaring more than 60% so far this year, stoking inflation pressures. In response to those pressures, the US Federal Reserve hiked interest rates in September for the first time since July 2023.
Consumers pay $4.33 a gallon for gasoline, compared to about $3.08 per gallon a year earlier, according to AAA.

According to CME FedWatch, traders now see a 37% likelihood the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates at its meeting in two weeks, up from 22% before the reading, and a 91% likelihood the central bank will lift rates at least a quarter-percentage point at its December meeting.

chains.t: ③ The AI Platform's Credit Test
steps: The buildout moved onto credit: CoreWeave carries $22 billion of bonds and $26 billion of loans; a June bond at 9.625% yielded 15% at last week's peak
The scare: Anthropic IPO investors weighed a ~$1.5T valuation, down from ~$2T; OpenAI's revenue was reported at ~$50 billion, not ~$70 billion
The repair: a sell-side upgrade has not reversed the move — the stock is still down about a quarter over two weeks
The test: Meta and Tesla report Wednesday, with Lam and Texas Instruments this week — capex guidance is the number that matters
chains.d: The AI platform's year: capex compounding on credit — October's stress test was a financing scare; the earnings week is the answer.

news.fact: Selling has been particularly intense in CoreWeave, which has issued $22 billion of bonds and $26 billion of loans, according to LSEG data. A CoreWeave bond that was issued in June yielding 9.625% recently yielded 15%.

A little over a week after it was reported that OpenAI's annualized revenue was approaching $70 billion, the AI lab is said to have told investors the real figure is some $20 billion lower — 'approaching $50 billion.'

Some current Anthropic investors and prospective investors in its upcoming initial public offering are weighing a lower valuation for the AI company after its latest financial disclosures, with some discussing a valuation of around $1.5 trillion, down from roughly $2 trillion previously expected.
